info.name: RiceFlow Third-Party APIs
info.description:
The third-party (outside) APIs RiceFlow uses, with the same parameters the system sends. Point: Panabo City (7.3086, 125.6830).

| Service | What RiceFlow gets | Key? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open-Meteo Forecast | 7-day weather for the scan; hourly forecast for the weather card and guide warnings | No | Backend |
| Open-Meteo Archive | Past rainfall: seasonal and monthly | No | Backend |
| Open-Meteo Elevation | Farm elevation | No | Backend |
| **OpenLandMap-soildb** (via Zenodo) | **Main soil source**: pH, texture, organic matter, bulk density. Downloaded once for Panabo, read locally at every scan | No | Backend |
| ISRIC SoilGrids (REST + WMS) | Backup soil values | No | Backend |
| OpenStreetMap Nominatim + tiles | Place names and the background map | No (User-Agent) | Admin website |
| Google Gemini | GeoRice AI chat and problem advice | Yes | Backend |

**Also used, but not REST APIs you can call in Postman:**
- **Google Maps SDK for Android**: the map where the farmer pins the farm (in the app, with a Google Maps API key).
- **Resend**: sends the forgot-password code email from noreply@riceflow.me over SMTP (`smtp.resend.com`).
- **Data files downloaded once** (not called while the system runs): ESA WorldCover 2021 and Google Open Buildings (pin checks for roads, buildings and water), BSWM Philippine Soil Series (soil texture), and NAMRIA/PSA barangay boundaries.

Only the Gemini folder needs a key: set `gemini_api_key` in the collection variables (Current value).

item.name: 1. Open-Meteo (weather, rainfall, elevation)
item.description: Free weather API, no key, no sign-up (open-meteo.com, CC BY 4.0). Used by the backend in `apps/environmental/services/openmeteo.py` and `apps/environmental/views.py`.

item.name: Forecast: 7-day weather for the land scan

request.description:
**Used for:** the environmental scan. RiceFlow averages the 7 days into temperature, weekly rainfall, humidity, solar radiation, wind and sunshine hours, which feed the RSI score and the flood-risk check.

**Code:** `get_current_weather()`.

item.name: Forecast: hourly weather for the dashboard and guide warnings

request.description:
**Used for:** the weather card in the app and the planting guide's weather warnings (rain, wind, heat in the next 6/24/48 hours). The backend caches it for 10 minutes per ~1 km area, shared by all farmers.

**Code:** `WeatherForecastView`.

item.name: Archive: rainfall of the last 12 months

request.description:
**Used for:** seasonal rainfall in the scan. RiceFlow adds up the wet-season (May-Oct) and dry-season (Nov-Apr) rain of the last year, because the RSI rule expects a whole season (about 1,000-1,500 mm).

**Code:** `get_rainfall_summary()`.

item.name: Archive: average rain per month (3 years)

request.description:
**Used for:** the planting calendar (average rain for each month, January to December).

**Code:** `get_monthly_rainfall()`.

**Used for:** the farm's elevation in metres (90 m Copernicus DEM). It is an RSI factor and part of the flood-risk rule (rainfed farm below 50 m).

**Code:** `get_elevation()`.

item.name: 2. OpenLandMap-soildb (main soil source)
item.description:
**RiceFlow's main soil source.** OpenLandMap-soildb by OpenGeoHub: soil maps for 2020-2022, 0-30 cm depth, 120 m pixels, free, no key (CC BY 4.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15608972). The maps are published on **Zenodo**, so the API is Zenodo's records API: each request below returns one map's record and its file links.

**How RiceFlow uses it:** `python manage.py load_openlandmap` downloads the Panabo City part of these 6 maps once and saves it on the server. Every scan then reads the soil from that saved file in about a second, with no internet call, so scans keep working when outside soil services are down. A scan shows `soil_source: "openlandmap"` (see GET /api/environmental/history/{farm_id}/ on RiceFlow's own API).

OpenLandMap has no nitrogen or CEC maps: those two use default values.

**Code:** `apps/environmental/management/commands/load_openlandmap.py` (download), `apps/environmental/services/openlandmap.py` (read at scan time).

request.description:
**Map:** soil pH. **RiceFlow uses it for:** soil pH, an RSI factor.

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

**Map:** clay %. **RiceFlow uses it for:** soil texture (with sand and silt).

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

**Map:** sand %. **RiceFlow uses it for:** soil texture (with clay and silt).

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

**Map:** silt %. **RiceFlow uses it for:** soil texture (with clay and sand).

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

**Map:** organic carbon. **RiceFlow uses it for:** organic matter (organic carbon x 1.724), an RSI factor.

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

**Map:** bulk density. **RiceFlow uses it for:** bulk density of the soil.

The record's `files` list has the map files; RiceFlow reads the mean map for 2020-2022.

item.name: 3. ISRIC SoilGrids (backup soil source)
item.description:
**Backup only.** Called when a farm pin is outside the saved OpenLandMap area, or the saved file is missing. Free, no key (CC BY 4.0). The REST API is slow and is paused at times, so the WMS map server is the second backup, and default values are the last.

**Code:** `get_soil_data()` in `apps/environmental/services/soilgrids.py`.

item.name: SoilGrids REST: soil at a point

request.description:
**Used for:** backup soil values when a point is outside the saved OpenLandMap area. RiceFlow takes the median (Q0.5) of the top 30 cm, weighted by layer thickness. Can be slow (up to 40 s) or paused; the scan waits at most 20 s.

**Code:** `apps/environmental/services/soilgrids.py`.

item.name: SoilGrids WMS: one value (when the REST API is paused)

request.description:
**Used for:** the same SoilGrids maps through the map server, when the REST API is down. Returns HTML; RiceFlow reads the number in it (pH x 10, so 55 = pH 5.5).

**Code:** `_wms_median()` in `apps/environmental/services/soilgrids.py`.

item.name: 4. OpenStreetMap (admin website map)
item.description: Free OpenStreetMap services, no key. Used by the admin website. OSM asks every app to identify itself (User-Agent) and to stay under 1 request per second.

item.name: Nominatim: place name of a farm pin

request.description:
**Used for:** the admin website shows a readable place name for a farm pin, and the admin's System Health page checks that it is up. The farm's **barangay** is not from here: it comes from the official NAMRIA/PSA boundaries saved in the backend.

**Code:** `rice-flow-admin/src/services/geocode.js`, `SystemHealthView`. Postman needs the User-Agent header below, or OSM answers 403.

**Used for:** the background map of the admin website's Farm Map (Leaflet). Each tile is a 256 px PNG; this one is zoom 13 over Panabo City. Postman shows the image.

**Code:** `rice-flow-admin/src/pages/FarmMap.jsx`.

item.name: 5. Google Gemini (GeoRice AI)
item.description: Google's Gemini API, used for the AI chat and the problem advice. **Needs an API key**: paste it into the collection variable `gemini_api_key` (Current value only, never share it). Free tier: about 20 answers a day per model, shared by all RiceFlow farmers, so send **List models** freely but **Ask Gemini** only once.

item.name: List models (checks the key, no answer quota used)

request.description: **Used for:** showing the key works and which models it can use. RiceFlow tries, in order: gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash.

**Used for:** GeoRice AI. RiceFlow sends the farmer's question with the farm's scan, variety, crop day, current guide step and weather, and first searches the DA-PhilRice booklets with Gemini File Search (the backend adds `tools: [{fileSearch: ...}]`). The key goes in the `x-goog-api-key` header, never in the URL.

**Code:** `apps/ai/views.py`. Uses 1 of the day's free answers.
